name: Authorisation adapter
purpose: The one module in the project that reads a Principal's roles, organisation ids, and claim bag to answer authorisation questions. Owns the mapping table from project-defined verbs onto the role and organisation-membership predicates that grant them. Exposes `can(principal, verb, subject?) -> boolean` and `assert(principal, verb, subject?) -> void | throw`. Downstream handlers speak verbs; the adapter is the only code that reasons in role and organisation vocabulary.
responsibilities: Load the project-authored verb-to-role mapping table once at construction; hold it as an in-memory map (AC-9104-1).
Evaluate `can(principal, verb)` as true when the intersection of the principal's roles and the mapping table's role set for the verb is non-empty (AC-9104-1).
Evaluate `can(principal, verb, subject)` with organisation scoping: when the subject carries `organisationId`, require that the principal's `organisationIds` array includes it (AC-9105-1, AC-9105-2).

Expose `assert(principal, verb, subject?)` that returns silently on grant and throws `AUTHZ_FORBIDDEN` naming the verb on refusal; the thrown error must not serialise principal claim material (AC-9104-2).
Confine the reading of `principal.roles`, `principal.organisationIds`, and `principal.claims` to this module and the claims mapper (TAC-1004); no handler reads those fields directly (AC-9104-3).
internalStructure: One stateless class over an injected mapping table. The mapping table is a project-authored module that exports `{ [verb: string]: { roles: string[] } }`. Extensions (custom predicates beyond role membership and organisation scoping) are project decisions that layer above the adapter's default reasoner; the blueprint does not name a predicate DSL.

interfaces.name: mappingTable
interfaces.description: Project-authored module exporting `{ [verb: string]: { roles: string[] } }`. A verb not present in the map evaluates to `false` on `can` and to throw on `assert`.

dependencies.name: Clerk claims mapper
dependencies.description: The reduction from raw Clerk claims onto the Principal shape the adapter consumes.

tradeoffs: Fixing the adapter's decision shape (role-set intersection plus optional organisation scoping) leaves fine-grained resource-level authorisation (per-record ACLs, dynamic ownership predicates) as a project decision layered above it. The blueprint's floor is verb-plus-organisation because that is what Clerk's own claim vocabulary supports out of the box; a project that needs richer predicates authors them as a project-side extension that consumes this adapter's output rather than replaces it.
